source.title_or_context: **Table 4** Main characteristics of each form of training (calisthenic/gradual mobilization, endurance, interval, strength, and respiratory)

table_assessment.assessment_notes: The two-part table contains source-defined exercise initiation, progression, intensity, duration, frequency, and non-recommendation instructions, alongside descriptive exercise effects and advantages. The mixture of normative and descriptive content prevents structural table-example readiness without row-level adjudication.

normative_assertions.notes: The inherited column header supplies the training modality; initiation is explicitly permitted once the patient is mobilized.

text_units.verbatim_text: Can be started as soon as the patient is mobilized

normative_assertions.notes: Exercise intensity is directed to increase according to perceived exertion.

text_units.verbatim_text: Increase in exercise intensity according to RPE

normative_assertions.notes: The table cell defines the initial intensity and duration progression point for continuous endurance training.

text_units.verbatim_text: Initial stage: intensity at low level (e.g. 40–50% VO2peak) until an exercise duration of 10–15 min is achieved.

entities.surface_form: Exercise duration and frequency of training

normative_assertions.notes: Progression is conditioned on symptoms and clinical status.

text_units.verbatim_text: Exercise duration and frequency of training is increased according to symptoms and clinical status

normative_assertions.notes: The recommendation explicitly applies to very deconditioned patients and provides a low-intensity interval example.
source_trigger_texts: It is recommended to start low and go slow

text_units.verbatim_text: It is recommended to start low and go slow [for the very deconditioned] e.g. start with alternation of shorter (10 s) bout of lower intensity exercise workload (50% of peak capacity) and longer recovery period (80 s) for 5–10 min

normative_assertions.notes: The row and column headers frame these values as initial resistance-training parameters.

text_units.verbatim_text:
Intensity: <30% 1-RM
Repetitions: 5–10
Frequency: 2–3 training sessions per week, 1–3 circuits during each session

normative_assertions.notes: Both intensity and session duration are progression targets in the initial stage.

text_units.verbatim_text: Initial stage: primary aim is to increase gradually the intensity (50 to >60 to >70% of VO2peak); the secondary aim is to increase sessions duration to 15–20 min, up to 30 min

entities.surface_form: duration of the bout of the strain

normative_assertions.notes: Duration and intensity are increased only when the training is well tolerated.
The recovery phase is shortened as part of progression.

text_units.verbatim_text: When well tolerated, first the duration of the bout of the strain (10–30 s) with shortening the recovery (80–60 s) phase, and therefore increasing the intensity (60–100%).

normative_assertions.notes: The source explicitly states the target session duration.

text_units.verbatim_text: The training session should last 15 up to 30 min

entities.surface_form: training frequency and duration per session

normative_assertions.notes: This is the subsequent progression step for interval training.

text_units.verbatim_text: Then the training frequency and duration per session are increased

normative_assertions.notes: The row supplies progression-stage resistance-training parameters.

text_units.verbatim_text:
Intensity: 30–50% 1-RM
RPE 12–13
Repetitions: 15–25
Frequency: 2–3 training sessions per week, 1 circuits during each session

normative_assertions.notes: The threshold is the source-defined optimal exercise-training intensity target.
The threshold applies to continuous endurance training.

text_units.verbatim_text:
Intensity: 40–60% 1-RM
RPE < 15
Repetitions: 8–15
Frequency: 2–3 training sessions per week, 1 circuits during each session

normative_assertions.notes: The source explicitly reports the absence of a specific recommendation for the inherited training modality.
The absence of a recommendation is explicitly attributed to insufficient available data and applies to the stated risk population.

text_units.verbatim_text: Owing to the lack of available data, the routine application of high-intensity interval training in moderate-to-high-risk cardiac patients cannot be recommended at this time and requires additional study

normative_assertions.notes: The absence of a recommendation is explicitly attributed to insufficient available data and applies to the stated risk population.

text_units.verbatim_text: Owing to the lack of available data, the routine application of resistance training in moderate-to-high-risk cardiac patients cannot be recommended at this time and requires additional study
